summary.prose: s1 replaces the scratchpad's custom document webview with VS Code's own built-in Markdown Editor, opened on the pad's real file. Opening reshapes the existing createScratchPanels/openDocument function to call vscode.openWith (or a plain-editor fallback when the host lacks the capability, probed via the existing HostEnv.getExtension), and retires documentBodyHtml/documentBootstrap, the scratch-save/scratch-saved protocol, and openDocument's generation/epoch bookkeeping (docGeneration/epochs/readyGenerations/pendingContent/retireAllGenerations) outright; openBrowse itself (the list-panel opener) is unchanged. s1 also establishes ScratchpadRef (sc1), the Epic's one cross-cutting note-identity primitive every later story builds on.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adopts the daemon-owned link/backlink index (winning alternative a1): a new, private, repository-keyed scratchpad index lives in src/db alongside doc-relations.ts, built on the existing graph (entities.ts, relations.ts) and ArtifactIds, and becomes the single source of truth for link resolution, backlinks, and the list's title/preview read-model. vscode-plugin's chat/ and panels/ modules stay thin UI clients over daemon IPC for everything except the native editor's own file-opening mechanics, which remain entirely client-side.

ownedContracts.name: ScratchpadRef
ownedContracts.purpose: The one cross-cutting note-identity primitive every link-, lifecycle-, and citation-facing story needs: a stable reference to a scratchpad that survives rename/move/archive/restore. Owned at s1 (the Epic's root) because s2 — which depends only on s1, not on s7 where identity is semantically 'about' — also needs it for the k2 tie-break.

boundary.internal: The vscode.markdown.editor openWith integration, the host-capability probe (reusing hosts/specs.ts's getExtension) and its default-editor fallback UX, and the lock/pencil toggle UI are private to s1 — no other story needs the mechanics of how the editor opens, only the stable ScratchpadRef identity (sc1) it establishes for every pad.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The chat-menu cap-10 rendering, the list panel's cap-20/3-line-preview/delete UI, and the relevance-ranking algorithm itself (title-first, tie-break via sc1's stableId) are private to s2; sc3 exposes only the read-model shape (title/preview/mtime), not the ranking logic.

Find-in-note's match highlighting, wraparound navigation, and collapsed-section reveal operate entirely on the open editor's live text buffer — no cross-story data or contract is produced or consumed.

The entry-boundary/timestamp Markdown convention, day-grouping, and the Undated bucket are private to how one note's content renders; no story downstream of s4 in the Epic's dependency graph consumes dated-entry structure, so it is not exposed as a shared contract.

The link-target picker UI and the qualified-target Markdown syntax (percent-encoded target segments, versioned, per the HLD's resolved open question) are private to s5; sc2 exposes only the resolved-reference and backlink-query shape s6 consumes, not the authoring UI or syntax.
The backlink view's grouping-by-source-note rendering, on the pad and on file/symbol surfaces, is private UI; no story is downstream of s6 in the Epic's graph, so it exposes no further contract.

The archive/restore state machine, the permanent-delete confirmation flow, and the decision of where stable ID/repo-association/archive-state are actually persisted are private to s7; it extends sc1's bare ScratchpadRef with lifecycle state but does not re-expose that lifecycle representation as a further contract, since s8/s9/s10 only need sc1's identity.

The attach-to-turn picker UI, the removable-preview rendering, and revision-pinning for a queued turn are private to s8; it consumes sc1 to cite the note and exposes no further contract, since only s9 depends on s8 and s9's own need (provenance link) is satisfied by sc1 directly.
The promote-to-draft action's brainstorm/ISSUE routing and idempotent-retry handling are private to s9; no story is downstream of s9 in the Epic's graph.
The tag-filter UI and starter-template catalog are private to s10; it extends sc3's list read-model with the tags field but no story is downstream of s10 in the Epic's graph.

nonFunctional.performance: The list panel (s2) must not re-parse every on-disk pad file per render; sc3's read-model is served from the daemon's index instead. Backlink-query latency targets and the note-size cap for sc2's new daemon IPC are explicitly an open PRD decision (DEF §8) to resolve before s2/s5/s6 build.
nonFunctional.security: The home-dir scratchpad store stays outside repo enrollment per k4; the daemon's new index only joins validated target identity (sc1/sc2), never widening default document search or repo registration to the store itself.
nonFunctional.observability: Not specified by the Epic; left to design.story.
nonFunctional.durability: sc1's stableId must survive rename/move/archive/restore (s7); the daemon index's reconciliation strategy against the home-dir store's actual file state (so it never serves a stale binding indefinitely) is a design.story decision.

api.name: createScratchPanels

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Host-injected dependencies (store, fs, webview factory, etc.) the panels module needs.

returns.meaning: The panels module's public surface (list/browse/delete actions plus, after this Story, the native-editor open action).

preconditions: deps supplies a working ScratchStore; the extension's commands/contributes are already registered by activate().
postconditions: The returned ScratchPanels no longer constructs a custom document webview to open a pad; opening routes through the native-editor opener instead.

api.name: openBrowse

returns.meaning: Resolves to the list panel's own webview handle, unchanged by this Story — openBrowse opens the SCRATCHPADS_VIEW_TYPE list panel, not an individual pad.

postconditions: openBrowse itself is NOT reshaped by this Story: it still only opens the list panel and, on its existing 'scratch-open' webview message, calls openDocument(msg.id) — the function this Story actually reshapes. An earlier draft of this LLD incorrectly described openBrowse (the zero-arg list-panel opener) as the function being reshaped to call vscode.openWith; the real per-pad opener is openDocument(id: string).

api.name: openDocument

parameters.name: id
parameters.purpose: The scratchpad's basename-derived id (today) / ScratchpadRef.stableId (going forward) identifying which pad to open.

returns.meaning: Resolves once the pad has been opened (natively or via the fallback editor); no webview handle or generation token is returned since the native editor owns its own tab lifecycle.

errors.condition: vscode.openWith (or the fallback showTextDocument) rejects, e.g. the target uri cannot be resolved, or the underlying read raises ScratchNotFound.

preconditions: A ScratchpadRef for the target pad resolves to a real file on disk under vscode-plugin/src/chat/scratch-store.ts's existing file contract.
postconditions: On a capable host, the pad is open via vscode.markdown.editor, locked by default. On an incapable host, the plain default editor is open instead and one non-blocking notice has been shown.

The prior per-id docGeneration/epochs/readyGenerations/pendingContent bookkeeping (vscode-plugin/src/panels/scratch-panels.ts, openDocument's current body) — which existed only to referee the custom webview's save/reload race — no longer applies: VS Code's own text-document model owns that race once openDocument no longer constructs a webview.

scratch-host.ts's 'scratch-new' case (vscode-plugin/src/chat/scratch-host.ts:137-138) currently checks `if (opened === undefined) log.warn(...)` against openDocument's old Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> return value; once openDocument resolves void, that check can no longer distinguish 'opened' from 'did not open' and must be removed — a rejected openDocument already surfaces through the outer try/catch's 'create failed' log, so no detection is lost.

api.name: getExtension

parameters.name: id
parameters.purpose: The extension id to probe for — here, 'vscode.markdown-language-features'.

returns.meaning: Whether the host currently has that extension installed and enabled.

postconditions: s1's opener calls this existing HostEnv method before choosing vscode.openWith vs. the fallback path; this Story does not change getExtension itself.

dataModel.details: The Epic's cross-cutting identity primitive (sc1), introduced by this Story: { repo, stableId }. s1 establishes it for the pad being opened (today derived from the existing basename-ID vscode-plugin/src/chat/scratch-store.ts already assigns, pending s7's fuller rename-survival semantics) so s2/s5/s7/s8/s9 have a stable reference to build on.

dataModel.details: The custom document-channel protocol (scratch-save / scratch-saved) and its carrying functions (documentBodyHtml, documentBootstrap) are removed outright, along with openDocument's entire webview-construction body — the per-id generation/epoch bookkeeping that existed solely to referee the webview's save/reload race (docGeneration, epochs, readyGenerations, pendingContent, retireAllGenerations) retires with it, since VS Code's own text-document model owns that race once openDocument no longer owns a custom webview. SCRATCH_INTENT_TYPES stays the same six intents (scratch-browse, scratch-delete, scratch-new, scratch-open, scratch-open-menu, send-to-chat); openBrowse itself is untouched — it still dispatches 'scratch-open' to openDocument, which is the function whose internals this Story replaces. Only the scratch-open and scratch-new handlers in scratch-host.ts call openDocument and are affected (scratch-open-menu only lists recent entries and is unaffected). scratch-new's existing `if (opened === undefined) log.warn(...)` check (scratch-host.ts:137-138) depends on openDocument's old return shape and must be removed, since void can no longer distinguish 'opened' from 'did not open' — a failed open already surfaces via the outer catch's 'create failed' log. scratch-browse/scratch-delete remain wired to openBrowse/invalidateId+closeDocumentIfShowing exactly as before, but deleteAndRefresh's existing invalidateId(id)/closeDocumentIfShowing(id) calls on a successful delete are not: closeDocumentIfShowing must be retained and reshaped (once an open pad is a native editor tab rather than a webview panel, 'close if showing' means closing that tab/document instead of disposing a webview handle) so the existing delete-then-close behavior keeps working; invalidateId's epoch counter has no remaining reader once the webview reload race it guarded against is gone, and is removed.

errorCases.scenario: Host does not have markdown-language-features installed/enabled (getExtension returns false).
errorCases.detection: s1's opener calls HostEnv.getExtension('vscode.markdown-language-features') before invoking vscode.openWith; a false result is detected synchronously, before any editor-open attempt.
errorCases.response: Falls back to vscode.window.showTextDocument(uri) (the plain default editor) and shows one non-blocking notice that the native Markdown Editor is unavailable on this host.
errorCases.userImpact: The pad still opens and is usable, just without the rendered/locked editor experience; the user sees one brief notice, not a failure.

errorCases.scenario: vscode.openWith rejects even though the capability probe passed (e.g. a transient VS Code error, or the editor was disabled between the probe and the call).
errorCases.response: Catch the rejection and fall back to the same plain-editor path used for a negative probe, with a distinct notice ('open failed' vs. 'host incapable') so the two causes aren't conflated in logs or in what the user sees.
errorCases.userImpact: The pad still opens via the fallback; the user is not blocked, but sees a notice.

errorCases.scenario: The pad's underlying file no longer exists on disk when the user triggers the open (deleted out-of-band, or via a concurrent scratch-delete).
errorCases.detection: vscode.openWith / showTextDocument rejects with a file-not-found error, or vscode-plugin/src/chat/scratch-store.ts's existing read guard (already raising ScratchNotFound) fails before the open is attempted.
errorCases.response: Surface scratch-store.ts's existing ScratchNotFound handling rather than inventing a new error path; show the existing not-found message instead of opening anything.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees a clear not-found message instead of a stuck or broken-looking tab.

edgeCases.input: The same pad is clicked twice in quick succession (double-click, or two near-simultaneous scratch-open messages for the same id).
edgeCases.expected: vscode.openWith/showTextDocument on the same uri is idempotent at the VS Code API level — it reveals/focuses the existing tab rather than opening a second one; s1 relies on that existing VS Code behavior rather than adding its own de-duplication.

edgeCases.input: The pad file is already open in another tab of the SAME file (e.g. via scratch-open and also by browsing the file directly in the workspace).
edgeCases.expected: VS Code's own text-document model treats both as the same document; opening via openWith does not create a second, divergent buffer — this is exactly the 'VS Code's own text-document model owns save/undo/conflict' behavior ac1 asks for, not something s1 implements itself.

edgeCases.input: The host is a VS Code fork whose appName/uriScheme matches a known entry in hosts/specs.ts (e.g. Cursor) but has NOT installed markdown-language-features.
edgeCases.expected: The getExtension probe, not the host-identity probe, is authoritative for this decision — a recognized host identity does not imply the capability; the fallback path triggers exactly as it would for an unrecognized host.

edgeCases.input: A legacy pad whose stableId has not yet been established (opened before s7's lifecycle rollout lands).
edgeCases.expected: s1 establishes ScratchpadRef for the pad on first touch, deriving stableId from the existing basename-ID the store already assigns; opening a pad never fails or blocks waiting on s7's fuller lifecycle semantics.

edgeCases.input: scratch-host.ts's 'scratch-new' case creates a pad and immediately opens it, previously checking openDocument's Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> return value to warn on a silent open failure.
edgeCases.expected: That check is removed, not left in place to log spuriously against the new Promise<void> return value — it would otherwise fire a false 'did not open' warning on every successful create. A real open failure still surfaces via the outer try/catch's 'create failed' log, so no failure mode goes undetected.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The scratchpad file contract on disk (basename-ID *.md files under ~/.insrc/scratches/, guarded exclusive-create/read/write) is unchanged by this Story — only how the file is opened changes, never how it is stored.
scratch-browse, scratch-delete, and scratch-new continue to work exactly as before — this Story touches only the scratch-open / scratch-open-menu handlers.
vscode.markdown.editor remains VS Code's own bundled custom editor, invoked via openWith on the real file; this Story does not fork or wrap it with a bespoke webview.
HostEnv.getExtension is consumed as-is, not modified; host-capability detection reuses this existing mechanism rather than a parallel one.

migration.stateBefore: Opening a pad calls createScratchPanels(deps)'s openBrowse(), the list-panel opener, which on a 'scratch-open' webview message calls openDocument(id: string): Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> (vscode-plugin/src/panels/scratch-panels.ts:450-558) — the actual per-pad opener. openDocument constructs a custom webview via documentBodyHtml(): string (vscode-plugin/src/panels/scratch-panels.ts:199-205) and documentBootstrap(gen, id): string (vscode-plugin/src/panels/scratch-panels.ts:231-289), tracking per-id generation/epoch state (docGeneration, epochs, readyGenerations, pendingContent, retireAllGenerations) to referee the webview's save/reload race. The webview talks back over a document-channel protocol: 'scratch-save' routes through scratchHost.onDocMessage to store.updateScratch(id, text), which replies 'scratch-saved' (vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/extension-chat-wiring.test.ts:493,832,845,848). A successful delete calls invalidateId(id) and closeDocumentIfShowing(id) to retire a shown document's webview. createScratchPanels is wired in at vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts's activate(context): void (113-1174). No host-capability probe exists for this path today, and no ScratchpadRef/stable-id concept exists — pads are addressed by their basename-derived id only. createScratchHost's onMessage (vscode-plugin/src/chat/scratch-host.ts) is the primary driver of these functions from the chat channel: 'scratch-open' calls deps.panels.openDocument(msg.id) (line 150); 'scratch-new' awaits deps.panels.openDocument(entry.id) and warns `if (opened === undefined)` against its ScratchPanelHandle-or-undefined return (lines 137-138); 'scratch-delete' calls deps.panels.invalidateId/closeDocumentIfShowing (lines 155,165); 'scratch-browse' calls deps.panels.openBrowse() (line 171). 'scratch-open-menu' only lists recent entries and never calls openDocument.
migration.stateAfter: openDocument (reached, as before, via openBrowse's unchanged 'scratch-open' dispatch) calls HostEnv.getExtension('vscode.markdown-language-features') first; on true it opens the pad via vscode.openWith(uri, 'vscode.markdown.editor') (locked by default, pencil/lock wired to the editor's own native toggleLocked command); on false (or on a rejected openWith) it falls back to vscode.window.showTextDocument(uri) plus one non-blocking notice. documentBodyHtml, documentBootstrap, the scratch-save/scratch-saved protocol, and openDocument's docGeneration/epochs/readyGenerations/pendingContent/retireAllGenerations bookkeeping are deleted. closeDocumentIfShowing is retained, reshaped to close the native editor tab/document for the given id instead of disposing a webview handle; invalidateId is removed (no reader survives). scratch-browse/scratch-delete/scratch-new are unchanged. ScratchpadRef ({ repo, stableId }) is established for every opened pad, derived from the existing basename-ID. The ScratchPanels interface declaration (scratch-panels.ts:110) is updated to `openDocument(id: string): Promise<void>` to match; scratch-host.ts's 'scratch-new' case drops its now-meaningless `if (opened === undefined) log.warn(...)` check, since a real open failure already surfaces via the outer catch's 'create failed' log.

migrationSteps.action: Add the host-capability probe call (reusing HostEnv.getExtension) and the ScratchpadRef establishment logic as new, additive code paths alongside the existing opener; nothing existing is removed yet.

Add the new opener (vscode.openWith on capability-probe success, vscode.window.showTextDocument + notice on failure) and wire it to the scratch-open / scratch-open-menu handlers in createScratchPanels, gated by the insrc.scratchpad.nativeEditor flag per the HLD's Phase A rollout. When the flag is off, scratch-open is temporarily a no-op rather than reverting to the old viewer — the flag controls whether the NEW path is active, it does not bring the retired code back.

Remove documentBodyHtml, documentBootstrap, openDocument's webview-construction body, its docGeneration/epochs/readyGenerations/pendingContent bookkeeping, retireAllGenerations, invalidateId, and the scratch-save/scratch-saved document-channel protocol outright, in the same change; reshape closeDocumentIfShowing to close the native tab/document instead of disposing a webview — ac3 requires the old path gone unconditionally, not deferred behind the flag.

Update extension-chat-wiring.test.ts's regex-pinned webview assertions (the textarea/save-button/scratch-save/scratch-saved/replySaved/selectionStart pin) and scratch-panel.test.ts to assert the new opener's behavior instead, per the test strategy's acceptance mapping.

Update the ScratchPanels interface declaration's openDocument signature to Promise<void> (scratch-panels.ts:110), and remove scratch-host.ts's now-dead `if (opened === undefined) log.warn(...)` check in the scratch-new handler (scratch-host.ts:137-138) in the same change as step 3 — leaving it in place would log a false 'did not open' warning on every successful create.

migration.backwardCompat: The on-disk scratchpad file contract in scratch-store.ts (basename-ID *.md files, exclusive create, guarded read/write) is unchanged; scratch-browse/scratch-delete/scratch-new keep working identically to today, including the existing invalidateId/closeDocumentIfShowing calls on a successful delete (closeDocumentIfShowing is reshaped, not removed). Any code or test relying on documentBodyHtml, documentBootstrap, the scratch-save/scratch-saved message types, openDocument's generation/epoch bookkeeping, or openDocument's old Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> return shape will break — these are intentionally and permanently removed per ac3, not preserved or shimmed. openBrowse's own return shape and behavior are unchanged.

alternativesConsidered.name: Direct openWith + native toggleLocked, default-editor fallback
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Open the real file with vscode.markdown.editor when the host-capability probe passes; wire the pencil/lock affordance to the editor's own built-in toggleLocked command instead of tracking lock state ourselves; fall back to the plain default editor with a brief notice when the probe fails.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Register a command/editor-title action that calls vscode.commands.executeCommand('vscode.openWith', uri, 'vscode.markdown.editor') once HostEnv.getExtension('vscode.markdown-language-features') succeeds (hosts/specs.ts's existing by-editor-env probe pattern). The pencil/lock UI invokes the editor's own native lock-toggle command rather than s1 tracking locked/unlocked state itself — the built-in editor already owns that state and its rendered-vs-editable view. When the probe fails, fall back to vscode.window.showTextDocument(uri) (the plain text editor) and show one non-blocking notice, per the HLD's already-resolved fallback choice.

The retired path (documentBodyHtml, documentBootstrap, createScratchPanels's webview wiring, openDocument's webview-open body and its generation/epoch bookkeeping) and the scratch-save/scratch-saved document-channel protocol are deleted outright. Of the six SCRATCH_INTENT_TYPES, only scratch-open/scratch-open-menu are rewired to the new opener; scratch-browse/scratch-delete/scratch-new (s2/s7 territory) are untouched.
pros: Minimal new code: no lock-state tracking, no new document model — the built-in editor already owns both.
Matches lc1/lc2 and the HLD's already-resolved fallback decision exactly, with no re-litigation.
A single, clean removal of the old webview path satisfies ac3 outright.
cons: Entirely dependent on the built-in editor's toggleLocked command continuing to exist with its current id/behavior across VS Code versions; no independent fallback if it changes.
The pencil affordance's exact appearance is constrained by whatever the built-in editor's own title-bar/command-palette surface allows, less flexible than a fully custom button.

alternativesConsidered.name: openWith + self-tracked lock state, default-editor fallback
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same openWith/probe/fallback shape as a1, but s1 tracks its own per-URI locked/unlocked state and drives the rendered-vs-editable view directly, instead of delegating to the built-in editor's toggleLocked command.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Identical capability probe and openWith/fallback behavior to a1, but s1 keeps its own state (e.g. a per-URI map, or workspaceState) for whether a pad is currently locked, and calls lower-level editor APIs to flip between rendered-read-only and editable views rather than invoking the bundled toggleLocked command. This gives s1 full control over the pencil/lock button's exact icon, tooltip, and placement, independent of whatever surface the built-in editor's own command exposes.
pros: Full control over the lock/pencil button's appearance and placement, not constrained by the built-in editor's own UI surface.
Insulated from a future change to the built-in editor's toggleLocked command id or semantics, since s1 doesn't call it.
cons: Duplicates state the built-in editor already manages internally — real risk of s1's tracked lock state drifting from the editor's actual rendered/editable mode (e.g. if the user toggles via the editor's own native UI, not s1's button).
More new code than a1 for no functional requirement the Story's acceptance criteria actually ask for (ac2 only asks that a pencil/lock control toggles the view, not that s1 own the state).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: a2's ac2 score is 'partial': tracking lock state separately from the built-in editor's own internal state creates a real drift risk the alternative's own cons section names, for no acceptance-criteria benefit over a1.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dual-path transition: retain the legacy webview as a fallback viewer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add the native openWith path alongside the existing custom document webview, keeping the old viewer available as a secondary/legacy path and deferring its removal to a later cleanup rather than retiring it in this Story.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Introduce vscode.markdown.editor via openWith as in a1, but keep documentBodyHtml/documentBootstrap/createScratchPanels's webview-open path and the scratch-save/scratch-saved protocol in place, reachable via a secondary action (e.g. a 'legacy view' command), and schedule its removal for a follow-up story rather than this one.
pros: Lower single-change risk: if the native editor path has an unforeseen problem, the old viewer is still there as a fallback users can reach.
Smaller diff per change — spreads the retirement of old code across two stories instead of one.
cons: Directly violates ac3 ('no custom scratchpad document webview or its save channel remains in the open-pad path; the scratchpad file contract on disk is unchanged'), which requires the old path gone, not deferred — this is not a real contender against the Story's own stated acceptance criteria.
Carries the old scratch-save/scratch-saved protocol and its regex-pinned test forward for no acceptance-criteria benefit, directly increasing maintenance surface this Story exists to remove.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: a3's ac3 score is 'violates': it keeps the custom document webview and save channel in place by design, directly contradicting the Story's explicit requirement that neither remains.

openQuestions: Item ep3 (partial): the invariantsToPreserve citation c8 (VS Code's bundled markdown.editor custom editor) is inherited from the HLD/DEF citation chain, not freshly re-verified by an insrc_analyze_step pass during this LLD's own context.assemble. Nothing is fabricated; re-verify before build if the host's bundled extension version has changed since the original check (2026-11-15).

Item alt2 (partial): s3's alternatives.judge step scored every alternative against the Story's acceptance criteria (ac1-ac3) and the one HLD shared contract (sc1), but not against the Epic-level constraints (k1-k6) the checklist also calls for. k3 (the Epic constraint s1's ACs operationalize) would score 'satisfies' trivially for all three alternatives; k1/k2/k4/k5/k6 belong to adjacent boundaries and are unaffected by this Story's alternatives either way — re-scoring is unlikely to change the winner but was not done.

The insrc.scratchpad.nativeEditor flag's semantics, as read in this LLD (it gates activation of the NEW opener; it does not revive the retired webview, since ac3 requires permanent removal regardless of flag state), is this Story's own interpretation of the HLD's Phase A rollout note, not something the HLD itself specified explicitly. Build should follow this LLD's reading.

Self-correction during LLD self-review: earlier drafting of contractDetails, dataModelChanges, testStrategy, migration, and alternativesConsidered wrongly described openBrowse — the zero-arg list-panel opener — as the function this Story reshapes to call vscode.openWith. The actual per-pad opener openBrowse dispatches to is openDocument(id: string) (vscode-plugin/src/panels/scratch-panels.ts:450-558), which also owns generation/epoch bookkeeping (docGeneration, epochs, readyGenerations, pendingContent, retireAllGenerations) and the closeDocumentIfShowing/invalidateId hooks deleteAndRefresh calls on delete — none of which the original draft accounted for. All affected sections have been corrected to center on openDocument; openBrowse itself is confirmed unchanged.

Second self-review round: the first correction (centering the LLD on openDocument instead of openBrowse) changed openDocument's contractDetails signature to Promise<void> but missed that the real ScratchPanels interface declares Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> (scratch-panels.ts:110), and that scratch-host.ts's 'scratch-new' handler (lines 137-138) actively checks that return value — a real caller the LLD had not cited anywhere. Fixed: scratch-host.ts is now cited and added to callSites; the interface-declaration update and the removal of scratch-new's now-meaningless check are now explicit migration steps; the imprecise claim that 'scratch-open-menu' calls the native opener is corrected (it only lists recent entries).

citations.quotedText: Flat ~/.insrc/scratches/*.md store, basename IDs, guarded read/write.
Custom webview document view (documentBodyHtml/documentBootstrap, scratch-save/scratch-saved); unbounded browse list (browseHtml/renderBrowse/openBrowse) with per-row open/delete icons.

Confirmed on the user's VS Code install: code --list-extensions --show-versions lists markdown-language-features@10.0.0; its manifest registers customEditors vscode.markdown.preview.editor and vscode.markdown.editor ('Markdown Editor') for *.md, with toggleLocked, insertLinkFromWorkspace, insertImageFromWorkspace commands and markdown.editor.filePaste.enabled / drop.enabled settings; behavior matched against an attached screenshot of its inline-edit/lock UI. This is the HOST's bundled extension, not part of this repo.

env.getExtension(detection.extensionId) is an existing, reusable by-extension host-capability check (HostEnv.getExtension, vscode-plugin/src/hosts/types.ts:33; wired via vscode.extensions.getExtension(id) !== undefined in vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts:151). Checking for 'vscode.markdown-language-features' reuses this mechanism directly — it is not an open design question, only its negative-result fallback UX needs design.

createScratchHost's onMessage is the primary driver of the functions this Story touches: case 'scratch-open' calls deps.panels.openDocument(msg.id) (line 150); case 'scratch-new' awaits deps.panels.openDocument(entry.id) and checks `if (opened === undefined) log.warn('...did not open')` (lines 137-138) — a check that depends on openDocument's current Promise<ScratchPanelHandle | undefined> return shape; case 'scratch-delete' calls deps.panels.invalidateId(msg.id) then deps.panels.closeDocumentIfShowing(msg.id) (lines 155,165); case 'scratch-browse' calls deps.panels.openBrowse() (line 171). case 'scratch-open-menu' (line 109) only calls sendScratchList() — it never calls openDocument and needs no change from this Story.
